answer: Behavioral Echo Clustering. Each agent action emits a signed trace; the detector clusters traces by timing and phrasing overlap, flagging identities whose activity echoes another’s too closely. Unlike a sable filter that screens upfront, it runs after the fact on accumulated logs. Each flagged cluster must forge a distinct behavioral history—unique latency, vocabulary, task order—costing roughly 40 hours of genuine work per identity, so farms pay that per fake account.
